Occupational Therapy Assistant Full-time

Chatham Glen Healthcare & Rehabilitationhas an exciting opportunity for aFull-time Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA)

Facility Rated 5 Stars

We are looking for a dedicated OTA to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

AtChatham Glen Healthcare & Rehabilitation, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Plan and administer occupational therapy treatments for residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Occupational Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for occupational therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Occupational Therapist as appropriate.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, families, and caregivers.
  • Monitor and document patient responses to treatment interventions.
  • Complete all required documentation and forms in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy Assistant license inFL.
  • Current certification as a Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA).
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Occupational Therapist

Nexus at Berwyn has an exciting opportunity for a Occupational Therapist (OT)

We are looking for a dedicated OT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.At Nexus at Berwyn, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inMA.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license .
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Full-Time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Physical Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive patient evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans using a variety of evidence-based physical therapy techniques and interventions.
  • Create personalized rehabilitation programs designed to help patients achieve their functional goals and maximize independence.
  • Administer medically prescribed physical therapy treatments to relieve pain, improve or restore function, increase mobility, and promote healing.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team (IDT).
  • Provide clinical support, education, and guidance to patients, family members, and caregivers.
  • Collaborate with other members of the interdisciplinary team to promote coordinated, high-quality patient care.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Physical Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of physical therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with patients, families, caregivers, and members of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Physical Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Physical Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

WaterView Health & Rehab Centerhas an exciting opportunity for a Physical Therapist (PT)

$8,000 Sign-On Bonus Available for Full-Time position

We are looking for a dedicated PT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

AtWaterView Health & Rehab Center, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Physical Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive patient evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans using a variety of evidence-based physical therapy techniques and interventions.
  • Create personalized rehabilitation programs designed to help patients achieve their functional goals and maximize independence.
  • Administer medically prescribed physical therapy treatments to relieve pain, improve or restore function, increase mobility, and promote healing.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team (IDT).
  • Provide clinical support, education, and guidance to patients, family members, and caregivers.
  • Collaborate with other members of the interdisciplinary team to promote coordinated, high-quality patient care.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Physical Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of physical therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with patients, families, caregivers, and members of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Physical Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Physical Therapy license inVA.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates are welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Tracy LaNeve

Physical Therapist Full-Time

Cherry Brook Health Care Centerhas an exciting opportunity for aFull-Time Physical Therapist (PT)

We are looking for a dedicated PT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

AtCherry Brook Health Care Center, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Physical Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive patient evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans using a variety of evidence-based physical therapy techniques and interventions.
  • Create personalized rehabilitation programs designed to help patients achieve their functional goals and maximize independence.
  • Administer medically prescribed physical therapy treatments to relieve pain, improve or restore function, increase mobility, and promote healing.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team (IDT).
  • Provide clinical support, education, and guidance to patients, family members, and caregivers.
  • Collaborate with other members of the interdisciplinary team to promote coordinated, high-quality patient care.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Physical Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of physical therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with patients, families, caregivers, and members of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Physical Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Physical Therapy license inCT.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-Time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates are welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

Speech-Language Pathologist

New Carlton Rehabilitation & Nursing Centerhas an exciting opportunity for a Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP)to join our team

We're looking for a dedicated and compassionate SLP to join our in-house rehabilitation team and provide high-quality, person-centered care to our residents and patients. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside an experienced clinical team focused on helping each individual reach meaningful goals and maintain the highest level of independence possible.

AtNew Carlton Rehabilitation & Nursing Center, our rehabilitation team valuescompassion, collaboration, and clinical excellence. We work together to create individualized treatment plans and provide care that meets the unique needs of each resident and patient.

If you're looking for a supportive team where your clinical expertise can make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and patients for speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans focused on cognition, communication, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech-language pathology services in accordance with established plans of care.
  • Help residents and patients achieve their individualized cognitive, communication, and swallowing goals.
  • Provide education, training, and support for residents, families, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals regarding diagnostic swallowing procedures, including Modified Barium Swallow Studies (MBSS) and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES), as ordered and clinically indicated.
  • Apply sound clinical judgment and maintain skills consistent with current speech-language pathology standards of practice.
  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Speech-Language Pathologist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and patients with a variety of needs, abilities, and personalities.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, and the interdisciplinary team.
  • A genuine commitment to compassionate, patient-centered care.

Speech-Language Pathologist Requirements

  • Active and valid Speech-Language Pathology license .
  • Current ASHA certification.
  • Must be in good standing with applicable licensing boards and regulatory agencies.

Why Join Our Team?

  • opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates are welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive and collaborative clinical environment

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

We're looking for a dedicated and compassionate SLP to join our in-house rehabilitation team and provide high-quality, person-centered care to our residents and patients. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside an experienced clinical team focused on helping each individual reach meaningful goals and maintain the highest level of independence possible.

AtHeritage Grove Estates, our rehabilitation team valuescompassion, collaboration, and clinical excellence. We work together to create individualized treatment plans and provide care that meets the unique needs of each resident and patient.

If you're looking for a supportive team where your clinical expertise can make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and patients for speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans focused on cognition, communication, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech-language pathology services in accordance with established plans of care.
  • Help residents and patients achieve their individualized cognitive, communication, and swallowing goals.
  • Provide education, training, and support for residents, families, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals regarding diagnostic swallowing procedures, including Modified Barium Swallow Studies (MBSS) and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES), as ordered and clinically indicated.
  • Apply sound clinical judgment and maintain skills consistent with current speech-language pathology standards of practice.
  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Speech-Language Pathologist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and patients with a variety of needs, abilities, and personalities.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, and the interdisciplinary team.
  • A genuine commitment to compassionate, patient-centered care.

Speech-Language Pathologist Requirements

  • Active and valid Speech-Language Pathology license inKS.
  • Current ASHA certification.
  • Must be in good standing with applicable licensing boards and regulatory agencies.

Why Join Our Team?

  • Full-time opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates are welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive and collaborative clinical environment
